subject: Clarify default capture for requests/outputs and EU residency
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Sat, 7 Jun 2025 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests / streaming / outputs)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time today. We have a couple of implementation questions before we move to legal — specifically around what Redwood stores by default for requests and generated content when the account is configured to keep data in the EU. Our security team needs to sign off on the exact items that are persisted vs treated ephemeral. A few concrete items:

- For streaming responses (server-sent events / incremental tokens), do you persist partial-token streams, or only the final assembled response?
- Are the original prompts (user-supplied context) treated the same as model outputs for retention purposes?
- What is the default retention window for request/response payloads in hosted accounts, and are there customer controls to shorten or disable capture?
- Confirmation we can get a signed addendum limiting storage to the minimum required for debugging and billing.

We’re on a tight timeline — can you confirm behavior and provide any quick matrix or reference doc?

Thanks,
Samir Khan
Security Lead, BrightBank

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Sat, 7 Jun 2025 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests / streaming / outputs)

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I’ve attached a short matrix that breaks this down by API surface and deployment mode. I’ll follow up with Kimberly for the EU residency pieces and the addendum.

- Streaming: we do not persist interim token chunks by default. For hosted accounts, partial frames are buffered transiently in-memory at the edge while the stream is active; only the final assembled response (post-stream completion) is recorded as an artifact for debugging and quality unless the customer has enabled advanced transcript capture.

- Prompts vs outputs: prompts (the user-supplied request text) and outputs (model-generated text) are classified differently in our internal taxonomy, but both can be captured by default. Prompts are kept for a shorter default horizon than outputs (see matrix). If a customer opts into stricter privacy mode we can disable prompt persistence while still retaining minimal telemetry for billing and rate-limiting.

- Default retention window: for Hosted (default) accounts we retain full request/response payloads for 30 days for debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. Prompt contexts (input-only) are by default retained for 14 days unless the customer configures otherwise. These are conservative defaults designed to support incident investigation and model regressions; Dedicated and Private deployments are configurable per-contract.

- Customer controls: customers can: 1) set the residency region flag (EU/US/APAC) to pin storage; 2) enable the \"privacy-min\" profile to suppress prompt capture; 3) call the purge API to delete captured records on demand; and 4) request a signed SLA addendum limiting default retention. For Private deployments we can disable capture entirely at install.

I’ve attached the redwood-data-retention-matrix.csv with the per-endpoint defaults and the suggested config knobs. If you’d like, we can run a short call to walk through a sample flow with your security team.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightbank.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Jun 2025 14:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests / streaming / outputs)

Adding a quick note on residency and deletion mechanics from the infra side.

- EU residency: when an account has region=eu we ensure all persisted artifacts (requests, responses, logs, and derived telemetry) are stored in our EU storage cluster (eu-west). We also prevent cross-region backups for those artifacts unless explicitly enabled via the customer portal.

- Deletion / purge: auto-purge runs daily for expired items; retention windows are enforced at the storage layer. Customers may also call the admin purge endpoint (documented link below) which queues a targeted deletion job (audit trail retained for compliance). For outright emergency removal we offer a manual deletion run with a signed order; turnaround SLA is in the addendum.

- Attachments & exports: any artifacts exported via support (for troubleshooting) are tracked and require an export ticket; exports are redacted by default to remove PII unless the customer authorizes full export.

I’ve uploaded a draft SLA addendum we typically use for banking customers — it’s attached as SLA-addendum-BrightBank.pdf. If BrightBank signs, we can commit to a 7-day final deletion SLA for specified artifact classes (subject to legal review).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@brightbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 8 Jun 2025 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests / streaming / outputs)

Karthik / Kimberly — this is helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups: could you confirm the purge API endpoint and provide the HubSpot deal link so legal can tie the addendum to the contract? Also please send the DocuSign link for the SLA addendum.

If you can turn around the DocuSign today we’ll aim to get procurement to countersign.

Regards,
Samir
Security Lead, BrightBank
